# Your task: extend the M31 master leftward until it fades to sky

`<ARCH>` = `/Volumes/Logic Pro/Float Originals Archive` (800 GB free). Raw/large intermediates go there, NEVER in the repo — the internal disk has ~14 GB free.

## State (verified — files exist as described)
- Shipping master: `<ARCH>/root/m31_andromeda_hubble_mosaic_recut_v2_tiled.tif` (14520x7795, 363 MB). Its mask is `..._v2_tiled_mask.png`. Rick called this master "fantastic" — do not regress it.
- The un-suffixed `m31_andromeda_hubble_mosaic_recut_filled.tif` / `_recut_tiled.tif` are SUPERSEDED artifacts from a subagent collision. Ignore them entirely. Only the `_v2_` line is good.
- Ground-based reference for the extension: `<ARCH>/root/m31-mosaic-with-groundbased-image-jpg.webp` and possibly `<ARCH>/root/m31_andromeda_hubble_mosaic_crop_extL.tif`. Inspect both before choosing.
- Relevant scripts (read their docstrings — they encode hard-won lessons): `upscale/m31_recut_tilefill.py` (NEW, stage-3 native-res tiled fill, worked), `upscale/m31_extend_left.py` (the older single-1536px-pass approach), `upscale/m31_recut.py`, `upscale/m31_recut_fill.py`, `upscale/deepsky_pipeline.py`.

## The defect
Column-mean luminance vs a sky reference of 18.78 across the master:
```
lon      -71.4   -57.1   -21.4    0.0   +21.4   +57.1   +71.4
colmean   26.1    33.9    71.1   85.5    61.0    24.4    21.0
```
Right edge / sky ratio = 1.13 (clean, fades properly). LEFT edge ratio = 1.40 — the disc is CUT OFF, not ended. `build_canvas` clamps that 40% excess outward, so it smears. **Target: left edge / sky ratio ~= 1.15, matching the right.**

Why it matters, Rick verbatim: *"I want the galaxy to look wide enough that I have to turn my head slightly to either side to see the edges, but I want it to appear that it is in front of me, not wrapping around."* A left edge that never terminates works directly against that.

## Approach
Diffusion-based outpainting anchored on the registered ground-based frame — the same idea as `m31_extend_left.py`, but using the native-resolution tiled machinery from `m31_recut_tilefill.py` rather than one 1536-wide pass. Reuse that script's tiling code rather than reinventing it.

Two lessons from `m31_recut_tilefill.py` that cost real time; violating them will waste hours:
1. **Never name the subject in the prompt.** "intricate dark dust filaments and lanes" made the model paint literal black ink blots and a black feathery spider onto a bright init. Use texture-only wording plus anti-blob negatives.
2. **Black artifacts came mostly from the INIT, not the prompt.** No-data left black in the unmasked tile context gets copied by the model. Use nearest-valid fill + smoothing (a sigma=24 Gaussian hole-fill silently fails on large blobs — numerator and denominator both go to 0 at the centre) and assert the init has no exact-black holes before sampling.

## Compute
ComfyUI runs on the k8s cluster (`kubectl -n ai get deploy comfyui`), GPU is a V100 (compute capability 7.0). Ollama currently has 1 replica and shares that GPU — if you hit OOM or timeouts, scale `ollama` to 0 first (`kubectl -n ai scale deploy/ollama --replicas=0`) and **scale it back to 1 when you are done**. All upscaling must go through neural inference (ComfyUI), never Lanczos.

## HARD RULE — output namespacing
A previous session lost hours to two agents writing the SAME archive filenames concurrently. **Namespace every file you write with the suffix `_extL3`** (e.g. `m31_andromeda_hubble_mosaic_recut_v2_tiled_extL3.tif`). Never overwrite any existing file in `<ARCH>/root/`. Write scratch to `<ARCH>/derived/m31_extL3/`. Do NOT touch any `m16_*` directory under `<ARCH>/derived/` — another agent is reorganising those right now.

## Deliverables
1. The extended master, namespaced as above, with its mask.
2. A measured before/after column-mean table proving the left ratio moved toward ~1.15, using the same sky reference of 18.78 so the numbers are comparable to the table above.
3. A downsampled JPEG side-by-side (before | after) at a size Rick can open on a monitor, saved to `<ARCH>/derived/m31_extL3/`. **Rick has aphantasia — he cannot evaluate a verbal description of an image. A file he can open is mandatory, not optional.**
4. Update the MANIFEST in `upscale/deepsky_pipeline.py` (around line 168) — it currently points at `..._v2_filled.tif` with `fov_x=142.78`, which is stale. Point it at your new extended master. cd "/Users/rashford/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Developer/Float" && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF' && git log --oneline -1
Science pipeline, M31 recut tooling, planet bodies; §8a add-on packs

Code only — image assets and 3D models are deliberately left uncommitted
until the M31 master and the planet renders are finalised.

New capability: render deep-sky backdrops from measurements rather than
press JPEGs. science_fetch.py pulls calibrated level-3 products from MAST
with provenance; science_render.py maps FITS to RGB with every decision
switchable (mapping, stretch, blend, merge, despike). Calibrated MAST
products carry no copyright, unlike the CC BY 4.0 ESA press images the
library currently uses — that is the strategic reason for the pipeline,
not just image quality.

M31 recut chain: m31_recut.py -> m31_recut_fill.py -> m31_recut_tilefill.py.
The tiled stage regenerates no-data at native resolution in 768px tiles
instead of from one 1536px canvas, which measurably improved mid-band dust
structure. Both scripts' docstrings record the two lessons that cost the
most time: never name the subject in an inpainting prompt, and black
artifacts come from the init, not the prompt.

Spec: §8a defines add-on packs as instruments, not settings — a pack must
require photons the base data never captured. Open questions kept in §11 #15;
nothing here has been evaluated in a headset.

Planet bodies and selector, grounded-equirect cap outpainting, and triage
page updates come along as in-flight work.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
